did_you_know.text: Did you know? Saul did not settle for making personal plans to harm David; he also ordered his son Jonathan and his servants to kill him. Despite this, Jonathan continued to love David deeply.

Did you know? Jonathan planned to hide David in the field, speak with his father Saul, and then tell David the outcome of their conversation. In this way, he combined practical protection with an attempt to reconcile David and Saul.

Did you know? Jonathan reminded Saul that David had risked his life in battle against the Philistines and that the LORD had brought about a great victory for Israel through him. Therefore, he argued that there was no justification for killing David without cause and shedding innocent blood.

Did you know? Saul swore, “As surely as the LORD lives, David will not be put to death.” However, later in the same chapter he again tries to harm David, so the oath does not bring a permanent end to the pursuit.
Did you know? After David returned to serve Saul, war with the Philistines broke out again, and David struck them with a great blow. His military success once again aroused danger from Saul.

Did you know? Saul tried to pin David to the wall with a spear, but David managed to escape. This is the direct assassination attempt described in the chapter, and it occurred while David was playing music before Saul.
Did you know? Michal helped David escape through the window while Saul’s messengers were waiting at the house. This allowed David to flee during the night and escape the immediate danger.

Did you know? To delay the pursuers, Michal placed household idols in the bed, covered them with a garment, and put a goats’-hair cushion at the head of the bed. This created the appearance that someone was lying there.

Did you know? After fleeing, David went to Samuel at Ramah and told him everything Saul had done to him. The two of them stayed together at Naioth, a place associated in this chapter with a group of prophets.

Did you know? Saul’s messengers, and Saul himself, went to Naioth, but the Spirit of God came upon them, and they prophesied instead of carrying out their mission. At the end of the chapter, Saul is also described as prophesying before Samuel, giving rise to the saying, “Is Saul also among the prophets?”
